facts.text: The black-faced monarch is a songbird that lives along the eastern seaboard of Australia and in New Guinea.
facts.quote: The black-faced monarch (Monarcha melanopsis) is a passerine songbird in the family Monarchidae found along the eastern seaboard of Australia, and also New Guinea

facts.text: Most black-faced monarchs migrate to New Guinea during the austral winter, from May to August.
facts.quote: (where most birds migrate to during the austral winter; May to August)

facts.text: The black-faced monarch is grey with rufous underparts.
facts.quote: The black-faced monarch is grey, with rufous underparts

facts.text: Mature black-faced monarchs have a black patch on the face.
facts.quote: mature birds have a black patch on the face

facts.text: The black-faced monarch prefers rainforest and wet forest.
facts.quote: The preferred habitat is rainforest and wet forest.

facts.text: The black-faced monarch's scientific name comes from Ancient Greek words meaning black face.
facts.quote: The specific name is from the Ancient Greek words melas "black" and ops "face".

facts.text: Alternate names for the black-faced monarch include the black-faced flycatcher and the pearly-winged monarch.
facts.quote: Alternate names include the  "black-faced flycatcher", "carinated flycatcher", "grey-winged monarch"

facts.text: The black-faced monarch is most closely related to the black-winged monarch.
facts.quote: Within the genus, it is most closely related to the black-winged monarch (Monarcha frater).

facts.text: The species has no recognised subspecies, making it monotypic.
facts.quote: The species is monotypic: no subspecies are recognised.

facts.text: "Black-faced monarch" is the official common name designated by the International Ornithologists' Union.
facts.quote: "Black-faced monarch"  has been designated as the official common name for the species by the International Ornithologists' Union (IOC).
